title: HyperBank: sudden reserved throughput collapse — immediate mitigation & exec visibility
text:
HyperBank: sudden reserved throughput collapse — immediate mitigation & exec visibility

['From: HyperBank SRE <sre@hyperbank.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:03:22-08:00
Subject: Realtime alert: spike in 5xx + reserved throughput saturation

Rachel —

We started seeing an abrupt rise in 5xx responses for model endpoint redwood-infer-v2 around 08:50 PT. Token queues for our reserved pool for region us-west-2 climbed from ~40ms p50 to sustained 900ms+ tail, and several requests are now returning 502/504. We believe this correlates with a large batch job from a new partner hitting our production window at ~08:42.

Attached: grafana snapshot + a trace sample.

Immediate impact: 8% of requests in the last 10m are errors; latency p95 jumped to 1.2s (previous baseline 180ms). This is affecting customer-facing flows (card auth & reconciliation) — business is seeing failures.

Can you confirm whether we have reserved capacity bleed or noisy neighbor on the dedicated pool? HyperBank is on a reserved commitment (HB-2024-09) and is seeing rate-limited behavior even though their commit should cover current QPS.

Elena (HyperBank Ops) & Sam (HyperBank TPM) are looped in. Please treat as urgent.

— HyperBank SRE

Attachments:
- hyperbank_grafana_screenshot.png (image)
- request_trace_sample.json (text)', 'From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: HyperBank SRE <sre@hyperbank.com>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@hyperbank.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@hyperbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:18:05-08:00
Subject: RE: Realtime alert: spike in 5xx + reserved throughput saturation

Sam / Elena — thanks for the rapid heads-up and the traces. We see the same metrics in Console (linked). First, sorry for the disruption — we know this hits critical paths.

Short acknowledgements and immediate steps:
- I’m standing up an ops bridge with SRE (Dylan) and infra (Jonas) now.
- We’ll throttle the noisy batch and fail open to your hosted fallback if we can’t stabilize within 10m.
- Marissa, I’m asking for a sales-safe fallback offer (temporary hosted capacity + credit) we can present to HyperBank to avoid client impact.

Can HyperBank confirm: did the partner batch originate from an external integration or an internal scheduled job? Any ETA on reducing the burst?

I’ll update every 10 minutes on the bridge; sending an exec note after first triage.

Action items assigned:
- Dylan Brooks: triage reserved pool allocator + immediate kernel backoff plan (10m)
- Jonas Weber: surface any reservation drift or allocation mismatch (5m)
- Marissa Cole: prepare customer-facing mitigation and temporary credit terms (15m)

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Lead — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cell: +1 415-555-0191', 'From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@hyperbank.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@hyperbank.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T10:05:48-08:00
Subject: RE: Realtime alert: spike in 5xx + reserved throughput saturation

Sam / Elena — Marissa here (AM for HyperBank). First, we are sorry — this should not be happening while on a reserved plan. We’re escalating to our exec team and will propose temporary remediation while engineering stabilizes the pool.

Commercial mitigation offer (temporary, while we stabilize):
- Immediate hosted fallback to run critical card auth flows on a managed hosted variant we control (same model family) for up to 48 hours.
- Apply a one-week service credit equivalent to the impacted tokens while you are on the hosted fallback.
- Priority engineering support and a post-incident RCA within 72 hours.

If you need a contract amendment for burst capacity, I can expedite a short-term addendum (DocuSign) to cover committed burst windows going forward. I’ve opened HS-54721 and have the DocuSign link ready — we can sign in under 30 minutes.

Please confirm whether you accept the hosted fallback and credit; we’ll cutover the routes after you confirm and after engineering gives the green light that the fallback routes will accept traffic without increasing error rates.

— Marissa
Account Director — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: sla_impact_table.xlsx (summary of projected token impact)', 'From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-05T15:42:10-08:00
Subject: RE: HyperBank: sudden reserved throughput collapse — immediate mitigation & exec visibility

Quick tech readout and recommended immediate mitigations (post-bridge):

Findings (initial):
- Allocation mismatch: the dedicated pool allocator incorrectly considered a set of cached KV entries as hot and allocated >30% of available slots to a bursting tenant that was outside of the reserved commit window.
- Prefix caching policy allowed a long-running prefix to hog KV slots and prevented efficient batching for other tenants, producing long queue times and 502s.

Immediate mitigations we implemented (09:25–10:00 PT):
1) Evict long-lived prefix cache entries for the offending tenant to free up KV slots (impact: immediate drop in p95; p95 back to ~350ms on non-impacted tenants).
2) Applied emergency allocation cap to any single tenant at 60% of pool for 30 mins.
3) Enabled graceful fallback routing for HyperBank to hosted-infer-spot (controlled variant) and warmed that variant with their key flows. We routed ~12% of traffic to the hosted fallback for 8 minutes as a safety valve while eviction propagated.

Next steps (0–24h):
- Today: full reservation audit (log + audit trail) to identify reservation drift root cause; ETA 6h.
- 24–72h: deploy patch to allocator to prevent cache-misclassification and add an automated cap when queue depth > X.
- Post-RCA: configuration change to prefix eviction heuristics and a queued-burst mitigation that will automatically failover to hosted pool for protected routes.

Risk notes: we must be careful with eviction thresholds to avoid increased cold-start latency for warm workloads. I recommend keeping the hosted fallback active for 24 hours while we complete the audit.

I’ll draft a concise exec summary for Vivek to send to HyperBank CTO/COO and include the minutes of the bridge + telemetry links.

— Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Quoted earlier messages included for context.']
